clue.text: In general for British, where's a good place to see eclipse?

definitions.meaning: Charles ... was the British commander who surrendered at Yorktown

definitions.text: where's a good place to see eclipse?
definitions.meaning: the reply to the question names the English county in the path of the 1999 total eclipse, followed by 'is'

explanation.surface: A quiz question asking about a general, then where the eclipse can best be viewed.
explanation.walkthrough: The 11 August 1999 total solar eclipse crossed Cornwall, England's south-western county; the second definition is the answer 'Cornwall is' to the question.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs to a British army officer famous for the American War of Independence surrender.

clue.text: Damage produced by son jumping into bed

indicators.note: the son leaps inside the bed, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a cot is a small bed

explanation.surface: A boy bouncing on his bed has caused some harm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What's the damage?' is colloquial for 'what does it come to?', so damage here means price.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally the damage is the bill or price you must pay.

clue.text: Bread and chocolate designed to fortify rally entrants

parts.note: a roll is a small bread loaf
a bar is a slab of chocolate

explanation.surface: Snacks of bread and chocolate handed out to give energy to drivers in a motor rally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fortify' suggests feeding the drivers; really it is the steel hoop protecting rally cars if they turn over.
explanation.definitionFit: A protective overhead bar strengthens the car body so crews survive a roll in motorsport.

clue.text: He cannot be expected to stand up for all his team-mates

definitions.text: He cannot be expected to stand up for all his team-mates

parts.words: He cannot be expected to stand up for all his team-mates
parts.note: reads as a disloyal colleague, but this cricket fielder crouches behind the stumps instead of standing

explanation.surface: A selfish player who won't defend his colleagues.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the player behind the batsman's stumps squats for most deliveries; he 'stands up' only to slow bowlers.
explanation.definitionFit: The cricket fielder behind the stumps usually crouches rather than standing upright.

clue.text: This child's parents work out what's necessary to admit

definitions.meaning: a child left alone after school because both parents are away at work carries a key to let themself in
the key that opens the front door lets someone in

explanation.surface: Someone whose parents' work lets them figure out what has to be confessed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work out' looks like 'solve', but means the parents are out at work.
explanation.definitionFit: A front-door key is the means of entry; the same word describes a child coming home to an empty house.

clue.text: At home, work in garden with old plant

parts.note: in means at home
to dig is to turn the soil in a garden

explanation.surface: Gardening at home with an old shrub.
explanation.definitionFit: The dye was obtained from a tropical shrub of the pea family that bears the same name.

clue.text: Part of year that's not hot — get the brandy

indicators.note: says the month appears without the letter for hot

parts.note: March is one month of the year
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: Spring isn't warm yet, so reach for a brandy.
explanation.walkthrough: MARC is spirit distilled from grape pressings.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a spirit distilled from the skins and pips left after winemaking, a kind of grape brandy.

clue.text: Part of opera on purpose set up for Strauss heroine

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece placed on another comes above it

parts.note: an aria is a solo song in an opera

indicators.note: in a down clue raising the word means it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: an end is an aim or purpose

explanation.surface: A section of an opera deliberately staged for a Strauss role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set up' turns END into DNE, written below ARIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Strauss wrote 'Ariadne auf Naxos', whose title character is the abandoned princess of Greek myth.

clue.text: Cashier not working in shop

indicators.note: the letters are put to work in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A cashier who is off duty while in the store.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges CASHIER plus NOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A store belonging to a group with many branches is a kind of retail outlet.

clue.text: Care to see Channel Islands with nobody about?

indicators.note: here the islands are held within the other piece

parts.note: solitude is the state of having no one around

explanation.surface: Is it a good idea to visit Jersey and Guernsey when nobody else is there?
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is the container signal here: the islands are held within the other piece. The Channel Islands are British islands off the coast of Normandy.
explanation.definitionFit: Anxious concern or attentiveness for someone is a synonym of care.

clue.text: Endorsement on passport is needed to enter state

indicators.note: the word is goes into the state abbreviation

parts.note: VA is the abbreviation for Virginia, a US state

explanation.surface: A stamp in your passport is required before crossing into a country.
explanation.definitionFit: A permit stamped into a travel document authorises entry to a country.

clue.text: Girl's unfinished appearance is wrong

indicators.note: the girl's title loses its final letter

parts.note: Miss is the title of a girl or unmarried woman
demeanour is outward bearing or appearance

explanation.surface: A young woman's half-dressed look is improper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' is a noun here: a wrongdoing.
explanation.definitionFit: A minor offence or misdeed is a wrong committed.

clue.text: Clever opening lost by Black

indicators.note: the black word drops its first letter

parts.note: sable is the heraldic term for black

explanation.surface: A smart first move given up by the black pieces in chess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opening' and 'Black' suggest chess; SABLE is heraldry's black, minus its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Being capable and skilful is a near synonym for clever.

clue.text: Having terror of hard study, with a blank crossword to fill in

indicators.note: the blank grid is slotted between the other pieces

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
a den is a private study room
an unfilled crossword is just a grid

explanation.surface: Someone dreading tough revision is given an empty puzzle to complete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to fill in' means the blank grid fills the gap between the two outer pieces; 'Having terror' must be read as an adjective phrase, tormented.
explanation.definitionFit: Being tormented or haunted by worry or fear is what the hyphenated word describes.

clue.text: Mariner, say, finds room on vessel

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: space means room
a craft is a boat or vessel

explanation.surface: A sailor discovers a berth aboard a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mariner' looks like a seaman, but NASA's Mariner probes flew to Mars and Venus.
explanation.definitionFit: Mariner was a series of American probes, so it is an example of a vehicle sent beyond Earth.

clue.text: An inclination to invest in favourite flyer

indicators.note: to invest is to place inside, so the slope goes within the favourite

parts.note: a pet is a favourite
rake is a slope or inclination, as of a stage

explanation.surface: A tendency to put money into the race favourite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Invest' and 'favourite' suggest betting; here invest means wrap around.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a small long-tailed parrot, so a bird that flies.

clue.text: See one's sunk in a depression for most of December

indicators.note: the see letter goes down into the hollow

parts.note: a dent is a hollow or depression
V stands for vide, Latin for see

explanation.surface: A bishop's see subsides into a hollow late in the year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' looks like a bishop's diocese; it is V for vide.
explanation.definitionFit: The church season of preparation before Christmas covers nearly all of the last month.

clue.text: Little creature aggressively reared

parts.note: seems to describe a child brought up to be violent, but describes an arachnid holding its stinging tail raised to attack

explanation.surface: A small child raised to be combative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reared' suggests upbringing; here it is the tail arched over the back.
explanation.definitionFit: This stinging arachnid famously curls its tail up over its body when threatened.

clue.text: I must leave tree to join in discussions

indicators.note: the letter I goes out of the tree

parts.note: a conifer is a cone-bearing tree

explanation.surface: Someone announces they will quit a tree to go and talk.
explanation.definitionFit: To consult together or deliberate is to take part in talks.

clue.text: Zola's heroine accepts one version of Bible for religious aim

indicators.note: the heroine takes the other letters inside her

parts.note: Nana is the title character of Emile Zola's novel
I is the Roman numeral one
RV is the Revised Version of the Bible

explanation.surface: A novelist's courtesan takes up a Bible translation for spiritual goals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepts' means the heroine takes the other pieces inside her. Zola's novel of 1880 is about a Paris courtesan.
explanation.definitionFit: In Buddhism the final goal is release from the cycle of rebirth, a spiritual target.

clue.text: Most nervous about running into cliff in cutter

indicators.note: the reversed piece goes inside the cliff

parts.note: a scar is a steep rocky cliff

indicators.note: means the shortened word turns round
only most of the word, without its last letter, is used

parts.note: timid means nervous

explanation.surface: The most anxious person running towards a cliff edge with a blade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most nervous' looks like a superlative but means most of a word for nervous; 'about' turns that to IMIT, which 'running into' puts inside the cliff word.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a curved oriental sword, so a blade that slashes.

clue.text: Putting an end to rewarding service

definitions.meaning: fitting a tip, an end piece, onto something
giving a waiter or driver a gratuity for good service

explanation.definitionFit: A gratuity rewards service; a tip is also a pointed end, so fitting one puts an end on.

clue.text: Laurel's given to a recited piece of verse

indicators.note: spoken out, these words make a single word

parts.note: Stan Laurel of Laurel and Hardy, so Laurel's followed by a gives Stan's a

explanation.surface: A Laurel and Hardy star is handed a poem to read.
explanation.walkthrough: Stan Laurel was the thin half of the comedy duo Laurel and Hardy.
explanation.definitionFit: A grouped set of lines forming a section of a poem is a verse unit.

clue.text: Sort of ant that likes to work a good deal?

definitions.text: Sort of ant that likes to work a good deal?

parts.words: Sort of ant that likes to work a good deal?
parts.note: an ant species nests in wood, and a woodworker shapes deal, a type of pine timber

explanation.surface: An insect that is a keen worker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A good deal' looks like 'a lot'; deal is softwood timber.
explanation.definitionFit: It names both a wood-boring ant and a tradesman who works with timber.

clue.text: Range of friends quietly replaced

indicators.note: the quiet letter is put back in another position

parts.note: pals are friends
P is piano, quietly in music

explanation.surface: A selection of chums is swapped around quietly.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a European mountain chain, and a chain of mountains is a range.

clue.text: In court, see fool

indicators.note: the word for see sits in the court abbreviation

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see

explanation.surface: At a trial, look at the idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: A clot is British slang for a stupid person, a dimwit.

clue.text: Semitic type has a supplier of alcohol turned back

indicators.note: the drinks counter is read in reverse

parts.note: a bar serves alcoholic drinks

explanation.surface: Someone who owns a pub that has been turned away.
explanation.definitionFit: Arabic speakers belong to the Semitic peoples, as do Hebrew speakers.

clue.text: Such action is almost all wrong

definitions.text: Such action is almost all wrong

indicators.note: the letters are put in a wrong order
the word loses its last letter

explanation.surface: Behaviour of this kind is nearly always bad.
explanation.walkthrough: ACTION, IS and AL (most of ALL) are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Conduct harmful to society is nearly always viewed as bad.

clue.text: What could be turned into relaxation?

indicators.note: the word may be made over into another by shifting its letters

explanation.surface: A riddle asking what might become rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A thaw is an easing of tension, as in diplomatic relations.

clue.text: Decline to correct pronunciation of old craftsman

indicators.note: says the words are spoken, not written

parts.note: to wane is to decline; to right something is to correct it

explanation.surface: Refusing to fix the way an old artisan's name is said.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decline' looks like 'refuse'; it means wane.
explanation.definitionFit: A wainwright built carts and wagons, a traditional trade.
